title: Payment Default and Termination under the SunPath Solar Lease
content:
## Section 7 — Late payment and default (SunPath Solar Lease)

**7.1 Late fee.** A monthly lease line still unpaid the grace period's number of calendar days after its due date carries the late fee once.

**7.2 Days past due.** The days past due of a lease are the calendar days, counted on the current date, since the due date of the oldest unpaid monthly lease line.

**7.3 Default notice.** When the days past due exceed the default threshold in days past due, a default notice is sent.

**7.4 Termination for default.** The lease may be terminated for default only when at least the default notice period in calendar days has passed since the default notice was sent. Counting starts the day after the notice date, and termination is allowed on the last counted day, provided the default is uncured. The system is then removed at the lessor's option. A lease terminated for default moves from active to terminated.

## How the notice period is counted

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Event that starts the clock | The sending of the default notice |
| Record that shows it | The date of the default notice in the lease's own notice records |
| Lease the notice must belong to | The same lease that is to be terminated |
| First counted day | The day after the notice date |
| Unit | Calendar days |
| Comparison | Termination not before the last counted day |
| Last counted day | Allowed — the boundary day itself qualifies |
| Further condition | The default is uncured |

The lease records decide the point: the date that counts is the date the default notice was sent as recorded for that lease, checked before the termination.

## Boundary cases, notice period of N calendar days

| Day, counted from the notice date | Counted day | Termination for default |
|---|---|---|
| The notice date itself | Not counted | Not allowed |
| The notice date plus N less one day | Day N less one | Not allowed |
| The notice date plus N days | Day N, the last counted day | Allowed, if the default is uncured |
| Any later day | Beyond day N | Allowed, if the default is uncured |

On the last counted day itself, a default that has been cured does not allow termination.

## Default notice threshold — boundary cases

With a default threshold of T days past due:

- T days past due: the threshold is reached but not exceeded, so this rule does not send a default notice.
- T plus one day past due: the threshold is exceeded and a default notice is sent.

## Late fee — points of judgement

- The fee attaches to a monthly lease line that is still unpaid when the grace period after its due date has run.
- It is charged once per line: a line that stays unpaid longer does not carry a second late fee.
- Days past due run from the due date of the oldest unpaid monthly lease line, so a payment that clears the oldest line moves the count to the next oldest unpaid line's due date.
